narrative.overview:
The explorer is printed, not rendered. It takes its material from the two-colour Czech Statistical Yearbook: a warm paper ground, near-black ink, and one petrol-blue second colour. Every chart is set as a yearbook plate, with a heavy double rule on top, a bold figure title, a grey unit line, the figure itself, and a small footer that ends in an italic source line. Each plate can flip into its ruled table. Separation comes from 1px hairline rules, never from boxes or card backgrounds, so the page reads as a ruled sheet rather than a grid of floating widgets.

The density is high and deliberate: small faceted multiples, a 13 px control size, tabular numerals in every place a number appears, and a persistent filter column that shows its live count at the top. Colour is spent with care. Petrol marks what the reader has selected or activated, and the darker petrol-deep is used only for the masthead band. All other colour is data colour, and each data colour has one fixed meaning.

Motion is small and practical. State changes use a 180 ms ease-out, the mobile filter drawer slides in over 220 ms, and everything collapses to instant changes under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, near-black ink, and one petrol second colour that means "selected / active".
The yearbook plate: a 2px + 1px ink rule, title, unit line, figure, and source footer, with a Chart / Table toggle.
Hairline rules instead of boxes, and crisp 1px axes.
One family (Source Sans 3) with tabular, lining numerals everywhere.
Data colours with fixed meanings that stay readable for colour-blind readers, backed up by line style or hatching.
Nothing disappears: excluded or unselected data stays visible as faint warm-grey context.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Petrol means "selected / active". If a control is not reporting a selection or an active state, it is ink on paper. Neutral actions like reset, retry, clear-selection and the All / None quick links never use petrol.

rules.name: The Nothing Disappears Rule
rules.body: Data excluded by a filter, a brush or a focus change stays on screen in context stone (or a light warm grey at low opacity on canvas). It never vanishes.

rules.name: The Redundant Encoding Rule
rules.body: No data colour carries meaning alone. The average is dashed, an incomplete year is dotted (1.5 3), grade 4 is hatched, and rise words are bold while fall words are regular weight.

rules.name: The Single Family Rule
rules.body: Source Sans 3 is the only family, and italic is reserved for the source line.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is set in tabular, lining figures so columns and axis labels line up.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest have no shadow. A shadow means a layer that floats above the sheet for a moment (a tooltip or the drawer), never a card.

dos: **Do** set every chart as a yearbook plate: a 2px + 1px ink rule, title, unit line, figure, a footer with an italic source line, and a Table toggle wherever the data has a table form.
**Do** keep petrol for selection and active state only, and give neutral actions ink or rule treatments.
**Do** keep excluded or deselected data visible in context stone instead of removing it.
**Do** back up every data colour with a second cue: dashes for averages, dots for incomplete years, hatching for grade 4, and weight for rising words.
**Do** use tabular, lining numerals and right-align numbers in tables.
**Do** separate regions with 1px rule or rule-soft hairlines and paper tone changes.
**Do** keep warnings and caveats inline in caution ochre, next to the chart they qualify.
donts: **Don't** put a chart in a rounded, shadowed card. Plates are ruled, not boxed.
**Don't** use petrol for decoration, headings, neutral buttons, or as a data series colour.
**Don't** draw the average or university reference as a solid line, or in any colour other than avg.
**Don't** add a second type family or a display face. Italic is for the source line only.
**Don't** put an uppercase label above a plate title. Uppercase tracking is for control-group legends only.
**Don't** use shadows on surfaces at rest. Only the tooltip and the mobile drawer float.
**Don't** use the grade ramp or rise / fall colours for anything other than grades and word movement.
